briefing.text: The hypothesis concerns only PIK3CA-mutant, HR+ patients. Filter on PIK3CA status (e.g. PIK3CA_PRE_TREATMENT_TUMOR or PIK3CA mutations) and BREAST_CANCER_SUBTYPE in data_clinical_patient.txt and run the PTEN-versus-outcome comparison in that subset. Report the all-patient result only as a sensitivity analysis.
briefing.reason: Including PIK3CA-wild-type or HER2+ patients would dilute or confound the PTEN effect the hypothesis is about.

briefing.text: Define PTEN loss-of-function per patient as the union of three things: truncating, splice or known-hotspot mutations (e.g. R130, R173) from data_mutations.txt; homozygous deletion (PTEN == -2) in data_cna.txt; and PTEN rows in data_sv.txt. Not every PTEN mutation is LoF. Synonymous, intronic or VUS missense calls in tumour-only samples may be germline or passenger. Use a strict LoF definition as primary and a broad one as sensitivity.
briefing.reason: Counting mutations alone undercounts PTEN-altered patients, and counting every variant misclassifies some. Either error changes the groups being compared.

briefing.text: Some panels (e.g. Sequenom, Guardant cfDNA) may not cover PTEN or detect deletions, so no PTEN call does not mean PTEN wild-type. Check data_gene_panel_matrix.txt and the platform of each sample. Exclude samples that do not profile PTEN from the denominators, and take CNA only from profiled (e.g. MSK-IMPACT) samples.
briefing.reason: Counting unprofiled samples as wild-type biases the comparison group.

briefing.text: Samples include pre-treatment tumour and cfDNA collected before, during and after treatment. Tabulate PTEN events by SAMPLE_COLLECTION_TIMEPOINT. Analyse baseline PTEN status against clinical benefit / weeks on study (primary resistance). Separately, report PTEN alterations that newly appear in on- or post-treatment samples as evidence on acquired resistance. Compare paired samples within the same patient, and do not count patients with several samples more than once.
briefing.reason: Mixing baseline predictors with alterations that emerge on treatment, or counting repeated samples, distorts any test of resistance.

briefing.text: Patients who stopped alpelisib for toxicity (OFF_STUDY_REASON) have short WEEKS_ON_STUDY for reasons unrelated to tumour resistance. Tabulate OFF_STUDY_REASON by PTEN status, and censor or exclude toxicity discontinuations. Prefer CLINICAL_BENEFIT or progression-driven endpoints.
briefing.reason: Using raw time on study mixes toxicity with resistance.

briefing.text: The cohort is small (about 50 patients) and few have PTEN alterations, so a non-significant Fisher or log-rank test is underpowered and is not by itself evidence that there is no association. Report the counts, the clinical benefit rates and the weeks on study for PTEN-LoF versus PTEN-intact patients, with the direction and size of the effect, not only a p-value. Where the data are too sparse to decide, weigh established biology as the task instructions say.
briefing.reason: The hypothesis claims there is no association, so how a null result is read directly decides the label.
